description: Machine-readable descriptor of the three EarthSciIO extensibility registries. Each registry is a name->implementation lookup. New backends register under a new name WITHOUT touching the Provider API. 'active' entries ship now; 'stub' entries are registered now (exercised via the registries by esio-9nb.8) and implemented later. The Provider depends only on the three interfaces named here.

transport.purpose: Fetch a resolved URL's bytes into the cache (conditional GET, auth, mirror failover). Bypassed entirely in offline mode.

entries.name: file
entries.notes: Expands ${EARTHSCIDATADIR} inside file:// templates; local copy into cache.

entries.name: cds
entries.notes: Copernicus CDS API v1: cds://<dataset>?<canonical-request-json> is submitted (POST .../execution), the job is polled to completion, and the result asset href is downloaded into the cache. Auth via the 'cds' realm (PRIVATE-TOKEN from ~/.cdsapirc or $CDSAPI_KEY).

entries.name: s3
entries.notes: Anonymous object GET: rewrites s3://<bucket>/<key> to regional virtual-hosted HTTPS (https://<bucket>.s3.<region>.amazonaws.com/<key>, region default us-east-2 via $EARTHSCI_S3_REGION/$AWS_REGION) and delegates to the http transport. No AWS SDK / SigV4; the s3:// URL stays canonical in the cache key + manifest.

format.purpose: Open a cached blob and return CF-decoded native-grid arrays keyed by file_variable. Does NOT remap variable names or apply unit_conversion (those stay in ESS).

entries.name: netcdf
entries.notes: CF decode: scale_factor/add_offset, _FillValue->NaN, time units/calendar retained raw. VARIABLE PROJECTION IS PUSHED DOWN in all three tracks: the loader's `variables` reach the reader, so an unrequested data variable is never decoded (a GEOS-FP A1 file carries 47 of them and a loader wants one) rather than being decoded and discarded. Coordinate variables are ALWAYS returned (they are the native grid the arrays live on); an EMPTY `variables` list reads every data variable, never none; a requested name absent from the blob is an error listing what is present, never a silently missing array. TEXT VARIABLES ARE `string` FIELDS in every track, never skipped by any of them (an ERA5 `expver`, a `char label(n)`, a NetCDF-4 `NC_STRING`): a `char` variable's last dimension is the string length exactly when nothing else claims it as an axis (no coordinate variable of its own, and every variable using it is a `char` using it last), so `char label(n, strlen)` is n NUL-stripped strings and a 1-D `char label(strlen)` on a private dimension is a scalar string, while a `char label(n)` beside a `float value(n)` stays n one-character strings. Only a compound/opaque/enum/vlen variable has no array reading at all, and requesting one of those by name is an error naming its type.

entries.name: geotiff
entries.notes: Raster bands via GDAL; Python ships first, Julia/Rust may lag (R5). No binary fixture committed yet (no GDAL/git-lfs here).

entries.name: csv
entries.notes: Points readers: numeric columns->float64 1-D arrays, others->string.

entries.name: shapefile
entries.notes: ESRI shapefile as a feature table, decoded by a third-party library per track (pyshp / Shapefile.jl / the `shapefile` crate). ONE ROW PER PART: a record's parts (outer ring + holes, mainland + islands) each become one row of the `index` axis with the .dbf attributes replicated, plus shape_index/part_index/n_parts. `geometry` is float64[index, vertex, xy] right-padded to the longest part by REPEATING the final vertex (esm-spec 8.6.1), vertices stored verbatim (closing vertex kept, winding untouched). xmin/ymin/xmax/ymax are the record's STORED bbox replicated to its parts. shape_type and (when a .prj is present) crs_wkt are one-element `meta` string fields. dbf dtypes: N/F->float64 (blank->NaN), L->bool, D->YYYYMMDD string, C/M->string; `numeric_columns` forces named C columns to float64. `nvert_max` pads geometry to exactly that many vertex slots so the DOCUMENT declares the vertex-axis length (a longer part is an error naming the row, never a truncation). A row is deleted iff its dbf flag byte is `*` (0x2A) -- any other byte, NUL included, is live -- and a deleted row drops its shape too. A shapefile is a FILE SET but the cache holds one blob, so the fetchable form is a .zip: `member` names the .shp inside it (sidecars are the same stem), absent `member` requires exactly one .shp, and a bare .shp decodes geometry only. `member`/`numeric_columns`/`nvert_max` are reader config and never part of the cache key. Reader-only: no reprojection, no unit conversion, no ring-orientation fix, no hole classification, no name remap.

entries.name: ff10
entries.notes: FF10 point long-format (SMOKE/Emissions.jl FF10_POINT); '#' header skipped; fixed 77-col schema; numeric->float64 (blank->NaN), ids/codes/text->string; zip member via reader `member` kwarg; multi-member via `members` (explicit list) and/or `member_glob` (fnmatch-style */?/[...], case-sensitive) -- union, deduplicated, rows concatenated in ascending lexicographic (byte) member-name order; absent explicit member / zero-match glob is an error; directory placeholder entries (names ending `/`) are never selected; `member` mutually exclusive with `members`/`member_glob`; `skip_header_row` drops exactly one asserted `country_cd` header line per selected input (first non-comment line's first field must equal `country_cd` case-insensitively, else error -- never silently drops a data row). None of member/members/member_glob/skip_header_row are part of the cache key (the blob is the whole zip). Reader-only: no pivot/unit-convert/FIPS-SCC-normalize/EGU-filter.

entries.name: parquet
entries.notes: Apache Parquet as a FLAT TABLE: every column becomes a rank-1 native field over `index`, keyed by its on-disk column name; a table has no coordinates. Decoded by a third-party library per track (arrow-rs's `parquet` crate in Rust, pyarrow in Python, Parquet2.jl in Julia). Parquet carries an explicit logical type per column, so the dtype is a total function of the Arrow type rather than CF attribute sniffing: Boolean->bool; Int8/Int16/Int32/UInt8/UInt16->int32 and Int64/UInt32/UInt64->int64 (the SAME narrow/wide split as the netcdf reader); Float16/32/64 and Decimal128/256->float64 (unscaled value / 10^scale); Utf8/LargeUtf8/Utf8View->string; Dictionary(_,V) reads as V, expanded; Null->float64 all-NaN. A uint64 above int64::MAX is an error naming the row, never a wraparound. TEMPORAL COLUMNS RIDE AS THEIR RAW INTEGER, undecoded (Date32/Time32->int32; Date64/Time64/Timestamp/Duration->int64): the Arrow unit and timezone are NOT applied, the same rule a CF time axis gets, because turning an epoch offset into an instant is ESS's job. Nested and binary columns (list/struct/map/union/binary) have no rank-1 reading: naming one in `variables` is an error, and in read-everything mode it is simply not a native field. NULL POLICY: a null in a float column is NaN (the fold CF _FillValue gets) and fill_value stays null; a null in an integer, string or boolean column is an ERROR naming the column and row, because those types have no NaN and any default would be a real value silently standing in for a missing one. The reader options `null_int` (an integer sentinel, substituted AND reported back in fill_value like a surviving CF integer fill) and `null_string` open that gate only when a document declares them; a boolean has no such option (declare the column in `float_columns` if a third state is meant). `float_columns` forces named columns to float64 whatever their on-disk type -- the Parquet twin of shapefile's `numeric_columns` -- and does double duty: an integer column whose missing cells must be NaN, AND a column of fixed-decimal TEXT (corpora needing byte-reproducible floats store them as strings rather than IEEE doubles; the MOVES snapshots write meanBaseRate as "261.000000000000"). Text is trimmed and parsed; blank->NaN (the FF10/shapefile rule); anything else unparseable is an error naming the column, row and text. COLUMN PROJECTION IS PUSHED DOWN: the loader's `variables` become a Parquet ProjectionMask so only those column chunks are read off disk (these tables are wide and a document typically wants three columns); empty `variables` reads every column; a requested name absent from the file is an error listing what is present. A zero-row file is TYPED, not absent -- the schema lives in the footer, so every column comes back empty with its declared dtype. None of float_columns/null_int/null_string enters the cache key (they are decode-side). Reader-only: no row selection, no filtering, no code mapping, no name remap, no unit conversion -- esm-spec 8.9 puts codes/record_filter/select/extent downstream of the decode, and `select` never reaches a whole-file reader at all.

entries.name: zarr
entries.notes: Store-backed Zarr v2 reader: parses per-array .zarray/.zattrs (no consolidated .zmetadata), fetches ONLY the chunk objects a lazy orthogonal selection intersects (each chunk its own object, keyed by sha256(object_url)), blosc/lz4+shuffle decode, C-order unpack, <f4/<f8 -> float64, dims from _ARRAY_DIMENSIONS, no coordinate arrays. fill_value is NOT mapped to NaN.

store.purpose: Physical home of the content-addressed cache (blobs/meta/locks). Realizes the cache layout; the cache key (sha256(resolved_url)) is store-independent.

entries.name: local
entries.notes: $EARTHSCIDATADIR filesystem: blobs/<key[:2]>/<key>.<ext>, meta/<key>.json, locks/<key>.lock, tmp/<uuid>.part. flock advisory lock + atomic rename.

entries.name: s3
entries.notes: Object-store backend (key->object). Conditional PUT / If-None-Match as the lock analog. Registered as a stub.
